r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding:
FAIL. BOM defect: correct, complete, well-evidenced (see r3/r5). D3 defect: the
Commander's reading is correct for the LITERAL symptom it was built to fix, but the
fix has an independently-confirmed regression on the DOMINANT real docstring shape
in this corpus, and that regression is worse information loss than the original bug.

=== Q1: is "summary = first paragraph, ends at first blank line (PEP 257)" the right
reading of D3? ===

Partially. It correctly fixes the demonstrated symptom: a short summary sentence
wrapped across 2 physical lines, followed by a blank line and a formal body (e.g.
Args:), used to be cut mid-sentence at the newline. `_first_paragraph` now joins
those lines and stops at the blank line -- verified correct against
`_git_rev_parse`-shaped and Args:-shaped fixtures.

But I checked real docstrings in this repo per the handoff's own instruction (Q1,
last sentence) and found the fix creates a NEW, larger regression for the shape
that actually dominates this codebase: a single dense multi-line paragraph with NO
blank line at all. A grep+AST scan of scripts/**/*.py alone found 132 docstrings
matching this shape (>=2 physical lines, no blank line, joined length >160 chars) --
e.g. scripts/agent_work_root.py:_git_rev_parse (3 lines, no blank line, 219 chars
joined), scripts/checklist_engine.py:_glob_to_regex (504 chars joined).

For this shape:
  OLD (baseline, pre-g8): summary = first physical line only (short, no truncation
    needed); body = doc_body_of (everything after line 1), UNTRUNCATED. Reader lost
    only the first line's worth of continuity between summary and body -- the
    original D3 symptom -- but every word of the docstring was still on the page.
  NEW (06fbc138): since there is no blank line, the ENTIRE docstring becomes "the
    first paragraph" -> the whole thing is joined into `summary`, hard-truncated to
    160 chars at the emit call sites (summary[:160]), and `doc_body_of` returns
    None (nothing follows the blank line, because there is no blank line). Every
    character past 160 is now GONE from the page with no indication more existed --
    not moved to body, not marked with an ellipsis, just dropped.

Confirmed directly against the actual generated pages in this worktree (map/ was
rebuilt post-fix at 2026-08-08 17:57, 4 minutes after the 06fbc138 commit):
  map/scripts.agent_work_root/_git_rev_parse.md line 8 ends mid-word:
    "...and lets OSError (g" -- the source docstring's own tail ("git absent / bad
    cwd) propagate -- both caught by the caller.") is gone, and no body section is
    rendered at all.
  map/scripts.checklist_engine/_glob_to_regex.md line 8 ends mid-clause:
    "...a single `*` matches within one segment (no `/`?" -- same pattern, same
    total loss, same silent truncation.

This directly contradicts DESIGN_SPEC.md's own stated intent for the summary field
(line 129, the redundancy rule): "DO carry the structural summary that saves
opening the file at all... signature and kind stay, they were the trial's measured
wins." A summary that silently amputates the back half of the only real content on
common pages does not save the reader from opening the file -- it actively misleads
them into thinking that's all there is.

I independently confirmed (by direct execution, not just reading) that truncation
IS applied after the join, not before -- the code is internally consistent with
what it does. The defect is not a coding bug; it is that the chosen RULE ("no blank
line = the whole docstring is one paragraph, hard-cut at 160, nothing recoverable
in body") is the wrong rule for this codebase's actual docstring population, which
this review's own Q1 explicitly asked me to check.

=== Q6: is the page-content change an improvement everywhere? ===

No. It is a clear improvement for the wrapped-summary+blank-line+body shape (the
demonstrated fixture case). It is a regression for the no-blank-line long-paragraph
shape, which my scan shows is several times more common in this repo's own source
(132 hits in scripts/ alone vs. the handful of Args:-style docstrings). Net effect
on the corpus this tool actually indexes is not unambiguously positive.

=== Recommended fix (small, does not reopen the whole gate) ===

When `_first_paragraph` finds no blank line, the current code sets body=None and
lets the summary emit sites truncate the whole doc to 160 chars with total loss of
the remainder. Either: (a) when no blank line exists, treat text past the 160-char
cut as the body (so nothing is silently dropped -- it just moves from summary to
body, symmetrical with the blank-line case), or (b) keep the hard truncation but
mark it explicitly (e.g. append an ellipsis) so a reader knows content was cut,
matching the honesty posture CREW_CONTEXT.md asks for elsewhere ("fail visibly
rather than emit plausible wrong output"). (a) is more consistent with the existing
design (body already exists as a channel for "the rest of the docstring") and
requires no new field.

This is a candidate eleventh Commander/crew error this run, if it holds: not the
BOM fix (correct), not the literal wrapped-summary-cut-mid-sentence fix (correct),
but the unstated assumption that "no blank line => the whole docstring is safely
truncatable" -- which is false for the majority of this repo's own docstrings.

r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding:
FAIL. Three of four boundary cases the handoff named are tested and I independently
confirmed they can fail; the fourth is untested despite being explicitly required.

=== Q2: do the new tests have teeth? YES, confirmed by direct mutation ===

I reverted `_first_paragraph` in scripts/code_map/extract.py to a naive line-based
split (paragraph = lines[0], body = "\n".join(lines[1:])) -- the exact pre-fix
shape -- and re-ran `python -m pytest tests/test_code_map.py -k "bom or docstring"
-q --color=no`. Result: 2 of 8 failed, 6 passed (not 8/8 green). The two failures
were `test_wrapped_summary_is_first_paragraph` (the core defect test) and
`test_wrapped_summary_no_body` (boundary case 2) -- both go RED on this mutation,
matching the commit message's claim. `test_one_line_docstring_has_no_body` and all
BOM tests correctly stayed green (a one-line docstring has nothing to wrap, so line-
split and paragraph-split agree -- that test isn't meant to catch this mutation).
Restored via `git checkout -- scripts/code_map/extract.py`; confirmed clean via
`git diff --quiet`. This mutation is not the crew's own falsifier (I did not read
their break-test script before writing mine) -- an independent attack, and it
caught the defect.

=== Q3: boundary cases -- 3 of 4 covered, 1 missing entirely ===

Handoff (g8-remediate.md and this review's own Q3) names four boundary cases:
1. One-line docstring, body None -- COVERED (test_one_line_docstring_has_no_body),
   passes at HEAD.
2. Wrapped summary, no blank line, no body -- entire thing is the summary, body
   None, remainder must not leak into body -- COVERED
   (test_wrapped_summary_no_body), and I confirmed above it goes RED under my
   mutation.
3. Wrapped summary + blank line + Args: -- COVERED
   (test_wrapped_summary_is_first_paragraph), confirmed RED under my mutation.
4. First paragraph over 160 chars, truncation applies after joining, not before --
   NOT COVERED. No test in tests/test_code_map.py asserts this. Grepped the whole
   test file for "160" and "truncat" -- zero hits outside an unrelated stale-tag
   test.

I verified case 4's underlying behavior is actually correct by direct execution
(doc_summary_of returns the full 216-char joined paragraph untruncated; each of the
three emit call sites then applies `summary[:160]` -- truncation genuinely happens
after the join). So this is not a functional bug, but it IS a real evidence gap:
the remediation handoff explicitly asked for a test on this case
("Watch the boundary cases... A docstring whose first paragraph exceeds 160
characters -- truncation still applies, after joining") and this review's own Q3
explicitly asks to confirm all four are covered and each can fail. One was silently
dropped with no note in either RESULT document. It is also the boundary case most
directly connected to the r1-handoff finding: a test built against a REAL (not
synthetic) >160-char no-blank-line docstring would likely have surfaced the body=
None-and-truncated-with-no-recovery behavior this review flags as a regression.

=== Q4: BOM fixture -- genuine bytes, confirmed RED without fix ===

Read tests/fixtures/bom_corpus/bom_sample.py as raw bytes directly (not via the
filename): first three bytes are b'\xef\xbb\xbf', the real UTF-8 BOM. Reverted BOM
stripping in scripts/code_map/extract.py (removed both `src.lstrip('﻿')`
lines) and re-ran `-k bom`: BOMParsingTests.test_bom_file_can_be_extracted goes RED
("BOM file should parse successfully (table non-None)" -- AssertionError, table is
None). Restored via `git checkout --`, confirmed clean via `git diff --quiet`. This
repo genuinely has zero BOM files outside the fixture (confirmed earlier by the
Commander and not re-disputed here), so the fixture is the only way this check can
ever go red, and it does.

=== Q5: checks.py find -- complete, no other second-parse site missed ===

Grepped scripts/code_map/*.py for every `ast.parse` call site: exactly three exist
in the whole module -- extract.py:371 (build_table), extract.py:1282 (run), and
checks.py:246 (SourceScan). All three now strip the BOM (confirmed by reading each
site in the current tree). The two other file-reads in checks.py (line 139 and 388)
read already-generated .md map pages, not corpus source files, so they are
correctly out of scope for this defect -- verified by reading their surrounding
code (MapModel.text and no_empty_pages).

(test_wrapped_summary_is_first_paragraph, test_wrapped_summary_no_body); the tests
have real teeth, not a check that cannot fail.

But per this review's own Q1 instruction to check real docstrings in this repo, I
found the chosen rule creates a NEW, larger information loss for the docstring
shape that actually dominates this codebase: a single dense multi-line paragraph
with NO blank line (132 such docstrings >160 chars found in scripts/**/*.py alone).
For that shape the whole docstring becomes "the summary", gets hard-truncated to
160 chars at the emit sites, and the body is None -- everything past 160 chars is
silently gone, where the OLD code preserved it untruncated in the body. Confirmed
directly against two real, already-regenerated map pages
(map/scripts.agent_work_root/_git_rev_parse.md,
map/scripts.checklist_engine/_glob_to_regex.md): both now cut off mid-word/mid-
clause with no body rendered and no indication content was lost. This contradicts
DESIGN_SPEC's own redundancy-rule intent for the summary field ("carry the
structural summary that saves opening the file at all"). Full reasoning and a small,
concrete fix recommendation (route 160+-char overflow into body when there is no
blank line, instead of dropping it) are in the r1-handoff finding.

Compounding evidence gap (r3-evidence): of the four boundary cases this gate's own
remediation handoff named, three are tested and I confirmed each goes red under a
targeted mutation; the fourth -- "first paragraph over 160 chars, truncation
applies after joining" -- has NO test anywhere in tests/test_code_map.py. I verified
the underlying truncation-after-join behavior IS correct by direct execution, so
this is a coverage gap rather than a second independent bug, but it is the exact
gap that would have surfaced the r1 regression had it been tested against a real
(not synthetic, short) >160-char no-blank-line docstring.

Fowler pass: one non-blocking flag (a one-line BOM-strip literally duplicated
across 3 call sites -- small, extractable next time a 4th site appears), eleven
smells absent, verify_fowler_pass.py exits 0.

Scope, constraints, reconciliation: all clean (r2, r4, r5 all PASS). No exclusion
violated, stdlib only, page headers and render report format both correct, no
architecture divergence needing Commander reconciliation beyond the r1 finding
itself. One triage candidate filed (this survey's tc1) for the broader design
question of whether a docstring summary should ever silently drop content past a
truncation limit, since it will recur on every future re-index.

VERDICT: the D3 fix as shipped is not a full fix -- it trades a narrow, rare defect
for a broader, more common one across the actual corpus this tool indexes. BLOCK,
with a scoped, concrete rework: teach _first_paragraph/emit sites to preserve
overflow past 160 chars in body when there is no blank line (or explicitly mark the
truncation), and add the missing >160-char boundary-case test against a REAL-shaped
(no-blank-line) docstring, not just the short synthetic one used elsewhere. BOM
defect and the rest of the D3 mechanics need no further work.

triage_candidates.statement:
g8 reviewer candidate: the doc-summary truncation policy silently drops content
when a docstring has no blank line and its first paragraph exceeds 160 chars
(summary[:160], body stays None -- see r1-handoff finding, confirmed against real
pages map/scripts.agent_work_root/_git_rev_parse.md and
map/scripts.checklist_engine/_glob_to_regex.md). Two design options: (a) route the
overflow past 160 chars into body when there is no blank line, so nothing is lost,
just relocated; or (b) mark the truncation explicitly (ellipsis) so a reader knows
content was cut. Worth deciding once, in DESIGN_SPEC, since it will recur every
time this tool re-indexes any corpus with dense single-paragraph docstrings
(confirmed common in this repo's own scripts/, and likely in f1Brainz too).
